title: TorchNPU NPUGraph capture synchronizes and does not prove replay speedup
summary: Entering torch.npu.graph synchronizes and empties caches before capture. Replay and update have separate gates, and the npugraphs backend patches Inductor entry points.

hardware: Ascend NPU via TorchNPU at this tag
software: Ascend/pytorch at 54e365d3e3614299bccd17f06916544c3880c9fc; not a tested pair with PyTorch v2.15.0
conditions: Question is NPUGraph Python capture, not the older allocator pin or vLLM-Ascend ACLGraph

claims.description: Capture entry synchronizes, optionally collects garbage when force_npugraph_gc is true, and empties device and host caches. The config default is false while its docstring calls true backward compatible.
update requires auto_dispatch_capture. Sharing a pool with an explicit stream requires the same stream. relaxed capture mode does not error on the malloc actions global mode rejects.

downstream_impact: vLLM-Ascend ACLGraph and TorchAir remain separate pins. Patching cudagraphify does not establish CUDA-graph semantics on NPU.
A capture that begins with a device sync should not be counted as overlapped launch without its own measurement.
recommendations: Treat downstream impact as a transfer hypothesis. No replay latency was measured.
validation_plan: A later authorized NPU run would compare capture_error_mode global versus relaxed on a known illegal malloc, and time replay only after a separate uncaptured baseline.
limitations: ACL runtime and npu/_graph_tree.py were not read. No NPU execution.
